bill.title: A joint resolution providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Department of Energy relating to "Energy Conservation Program for Appliance Standards: Certification Requirements, Labeling Requirements, and Enforcement Provisions for Certain Consumer Products and Commercial Equipment".
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources.
bill.officialSummary: This joint resolution nullifies the Energy Conservation Program for Appliance Standards: Certification Requirements, Labeling Requirements, and Enforcement Provisions for Certain Consumer Products and Commercial Equipment rule published by the Department of Energy (DOE) on October 9, 2024. Under the rule, DOE modified its regulations on the energy efficiency of certain types of consumer products (e.g., washing machines and dishwashers) and industrial equipment (e.g., computer room air conditioners). Specifically, it modified certification requirements, labeling requirements, and enforcement provisions for these products and equipment to (1) align reporting requirements with currently applicable energy conservation standards and test procedures, and (2) provide DOE with the information necessary to determine the appropriate classification of products for the application of standards.

classification.plainSummary: This joint resolution would block a Department of Energy rule published in October 2024 that updated certification, labeling, and enforcement requirements for energy-efficient appliances and equipment. The rule modified how manufacturers report compliance with energy standards for products like washing machines, dishwashers, and commercial air conditioners. If passed, the resolution would nullify these updated requirements and leave the previous regulatory framework in place.

industries.rationale: The rule directly governs certification and labeling obligations for manufacturers of consumer appliances and commercial equipment.
Retailers selling covered appliances would be affected by changes to labeling requirements and product classification standards.
Energy efficiency standards for appliances and equipment affect electricity demand patterns and utility planning.

plain.whatItDoes: This joint resolution would cancel the Energy Conservation Program for Appliance Standards: Certification Requirements, Labeling Requirements, and Enforcement Provisions for Certain Consumer Products and Commercial Equipment rule published by the Energy Department on October 9, 2024.
plain.everydayEffect: If it passed, the change would show up in what you can buy, and what it costs. Nothing has changed yet. Most bills never become law.

method.formula: score = Σ_industries ( donorShare(industry) × billWeight(industry) ), where billWeight = classifierConfidence / Σ classifierConfidence. Range 0–1, read as a weighted share of disclosed itemized money.

ordinary.text: They wrote this bill. Sponsoring a bill about your own district's industry is the ordinary case, not the odd one.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
